raw.query: SELECT experiment, window_name, lead_s, sla_metric, p99_ms, n_requests FROM provenance.v_pool_latency WHERE is_current AND quantile='p90' AND policy='forecast' AND sla_metric='encoder_delay' AND (window_name LIKE 'burst%' OR window_name='steady24h' OR (window_name IS NULL AND lead_s IN (15,30,45,165))) ORDER BY window_name, lead_s, p99_ms
raw.observed: Burst windows (forecast p90) p99 = 598.74, 880.66 (burst1), 588.37/630.62 (burst3), 588.37/663.62 (burst4), 588.37/656.74 (burst5) ms; steady24h calm = 733.64 AND 900.05 ms. Many bursts exceed 588; calm reaches 900>734.
raw.claimed: p99 unchanged at 588 ms service floor on every burst window; calm day below 734 ms
raw.evidence: Per-window burst rows for the p90 policy show p99 of 598-880 ms, not 588; calm steady24h hits 900 ms at rho25 — contradicts 'floor on every burst window' and 'below 734 on calm day'.
raw.fix: The L=15..165 invariance at 588 ms holds only for the pooled aggregate (window_name=NULL, issuetime) runs, not per-window. Burst windows exceed 588 ms (up to 880) and the calm steady window reaches 900 ms at rho25. Rephrase as aggregate-level lead-invariance, or restrict the burst/calm statement to the specific rho15 subset and drop 'every burst window'.
